profile.name: Scott Moss
profile.tagline: AI engineer, focused on AI safety research
profile.description: Scott Moss is an AI engineer focused on AI safety research. He shares what he learns and helps startups and enterprises adopt AI.
intro: I’ve built AI systems at {netflix} and as a two-time {yc} founder. Now my focus is AI safety research: how these systems fail, how to measure them and how to make them safe.
As an applied AI architect, I also help startups and enterprises adopt AI, from choosing the right problems to systems that hold up in production. And I create content sharing what I learn.

items.title: When everyone is aligned but the system fails
items.premise: Agents that each behave responsibly can still fail as a group: an incident everyone assumes someone else owns, or a warning that never reaches the one agent able to fix it. I’m running a simulated engineering org of 5 to 20 agents to measure how these failures grow with the team, and whether explicit ownership and escalation rules prevent them.

items.title: Safety memory for monitoring long-running agents
items.premise: A safety monitor can miss a violation when the evidence is spread across sessions, tools or agents: one agent reads a secret, another later sends it out, and each step looks harmless on its own. I’m testing whether a compact, persistent record of what matters for safety catches these as well as replaying the full history, at a fraction of the cost.
